question: Should OpenClaw add a native custom ASR/STT backend abstraction now, and should the first slice bridge native capture to existing Gateway media/provider contracts rather than adding a standalone native HTTP endpoint preference?
rationale: The missing capability is source-proven, but implementation choices affect native app UX, provider ownership, credentials, private-network trust, fallback behavior, and whether this becomes a new config surface or reuse of existing provider contracts.

options.title: Design Gateway-Backed Native ASR Seam
options.body: Keep Apple/Android platform speech as the default, start with one approved native flow such as macOS Push-to-Talk or mobile dictation, and route provider-backed transcription through existing Gateway media or realtime provider controls.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Trackers
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad umbrella while platform-specific issues such as macOS PTT and WebChat dictation carry implementation and proof separately.

options.title: Defer Native Custom ASR
options.body: Keep native voice capture on platform speech until maintainers define a broader voice-input provider plan and security model.

recommendation.title: Design Gateway-Backed Native ASR Seam
recommendation.body: Keep Apple/Android platform speech as the default, start with one approved native flow such as macOS Push-to-Talk or mobile dictation, and route provider-backed transcription through existing Gateway media or realtime provider controls.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history across native voice paths and is the best available owner for the platform-scope and product/API decision.
